Reviewed PR #2741 at head 65e391e0476231cd5f3243a502f9936d65ebf28c. The head sits on current main; no trial merge needed. Built locally: the new binary `stock_cut_twin` 7 passed / 0 failed, camcraft-sim lib 192 passed / 0 failed, clippy clean (-D warnings).

**The safety law: the twin never removes more than the f64 cut.** The law holds by construction. A twin claim needs `dist_f32 + margin < cap`. The margin (32 f32 epsilons of the tile scale, plus 1e-6 of the path length on the flat's golden-section path) bounds the f32-versus-f64 distance error, so a twin claim is always an f64 claim too. The parity test asserts `twin <= f64` with no tolerance per texel after the shared clamp at `-cap`, for both tools, over level, ramp, plunge and diagonal moves. The lower bound (`twin >= f64 - tol`) is pinned too, so the twin is not simply a no-op.

**Other checks.** The order-preserving key sorts every non-NaN f32 and round-trips; the max fold on keys answers bit for bit the same in reversed and rotated move order - the GPU `atomicMax` law. Refusals by name are pinned for all six tool kinds, arcs, tilted axes, zero-length moves and non-finite input. `run_twin` bounds-checks every write; a hand-made list that names a cell outside its brick gives an error, never a wrapped write. Files are under 400 lines. The decision file records the eight choices, including the one place the twin refuses where f64 accepts (a zero-length move).

**One note, no blocker.** An axis with exactly x = y = 0.0 and any positive finite z is treated as upright. A float tilt below that check would reach the f64 law as tilted while the twin cuts upright. The geometric difference is near 1e-9 rad times the reach, far inside the margin. If S2 wants the same law in WGSL, keep the check identical.

Effort: high, safety floor (stock simulation). P4, not P1 - no second review required.

Verdict: **merge-ready**.

Merge class: SAME. The head is `65e391e0476231cd5f3243a502f9936d65ebf28c`, the head that the review names (comment 7004919317). No commit came after that review. The head is on the current `main`. This merge relies on that review. The issue is P4, so one collaborator review is sufficient. Reviewed `feat` PRs merge at once by the standing order of the maintainer.
